title: Future plans: gaan + infinitive
text:
Here is the result of "fetch" for the Page with URL https://app.notion.com/p/401f89e5e0fc815bb7a8cd2d3d522186 as of 2026-10-22T22:50:31.389Z: {"Bronhoofdstuk":2,"Hoofdstukken":["https://app.notion.com/p/401f89e5e0fc8113b4facf9a197eabed"],"Inhoudsstatus":"Aanwezig","Onderwerp":"Future plans: gaan + infinitive","Ontbreekt":"","Type":"Grammatica","url":"https://app.notion.com/p/401f89e5e0fc815bb7a8cd2d3d522186"} null Gaan + infinitief Use a form of gaan followed by an infinitive to describe a plan, as in the city-trip exercise. ## Pattern Subject + gaan + other information + infinitive. - Ik ga winkelen. — I’m going to go shopping. - Wij gaan winkelen. — We’re going to go shopping. - Morgen gaan we winkelen. — Tomorrow we’re going shopping. This last sentence is supplied in the archive. ## Choose the right form - ik ga - jij/je gaat, u gaat, hij/zij gaat - wij/we, jullie, zij/ze gaan In a question with jij/je after the verb, drop the -t: Ga je winkelen? When morgen comes first, swap the verb and subject: Morgen gaan we …. Keep the infinitive at the end. Use the same pattern for the archive’s unfinished Mercator prompt; the missing photo means its exact intended answer cannot be recovered. ## Try it 1. Wij … morgen … . (gaan + winkelen) 2. Begin your answer to 1 with Morgen. 3. Ask a friend whether they are going shopping: … je … ? Answers 1. Wij gaan morgen winkelen. 2. Morgen gaan wij winkelen. 3. Ga je winkelen? ## Sources and chapter links Source and related chapters English study explanation written from the examples and learning goals in archived chapter 2. This is a new learning aid; the archive does not contain the missing original grammar handout.
